changes: original_meaning 保留拉丁语 solaris 的 gloss「属于太阳的」。
semantic_path 第二站 how 按 Etymonline 编年（1740 年靠太阳运转义 → 1915/1955/1964 年的能源术语群）替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "solar (adj.) mid-15c., \"of, pertaining to, or determined by the sun,\" from Latin solaris \"of the sun,\" from sol \"sun\""

Etymonline: "The meaning \"operated by means of the sun or its heat\" is from 1740; solar power is attested from 1915, solar cell as a photovoltaic device from 1955, solar panel, designed to absorb the sun's rays, is from 1964."
solar.mechanism_sentence: solar 是拉丁语 sol「太阳」的形容词，本义就是「太阳的」：1740 年起它兼管「靠太阳运转的」，20 世纪又一连领了太阳能、太阳能电池、太阳能板的新差事。

semantic_path.how: 太阳从『被描述的对象』变成『被利用的能源』：1740 年 solar 添『靠太阳或其热量运转』义，20 世纪术语连生——solar power（1915 年）、solar cell（1955 年）、solar panel（1964 年）——词库『太阳能的』即此。

changes: original_meaning 保留古英语 sōþian 的 gloss「证实，作证」，并写明其词基 sōþ『真』。
semantic_path 按两源一致的链条重建三站（证实 → 1560 年代附和宽慰 → 1690 年代安慰定型、1711 年减轻痛感），替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "soothe (v.) Middle English sothen, from Old English soðian \"show to be true, bear witness, offer confirmation\" (senses now obsolete), from soð \"true\" (see sooth). The sense of \"quiet, comfort, restore to tranquility,\" in reference to a person or animal, is by 1690s, via the notion of \"to assuage one by asserting that what he says is true,\" a sense attested from 1560s"
Etymonline: "The meaning \"reduce the intensity\" (of a pain, etc.) is from 1711."

Oxford: "In the 16th cent. the verb passed through the senses 'corroborate (a statement)', 'humour (a person) by expressing agreement' and 'flatter by one's assent', which led to the senses 'mollify, appease' (late 17th cent.)."
soothe.mechanism_sentence: soothe 的祖宗是「真」（古英语 sōþ）：它先在法庭边上「证实、作证」，16 世纪变成「顺着对方的话说、让他宽心」——哄顺了，就是安慰。

semantic_path.how: 桥在『顺着话证实』：1560 年代 soothe 指『肯定对方所说为真、借此宽慰他』——牛津排的链条是：证实（陈述）→ 随声附和（迁就其人）→ 以赞同奉承；作证的话术，滑成了哄人的话术。
1690 年代定型为『使（人或动物）安静、得慰藉』，1711 年添『减轻（疼痛等的）强度』——话说顺了，心平了，连身上的痛都跟着轻了；词库今义『安慰；使平静』即此。

changes: original_meaning 与古英语 sāwol 的 gloss 对齐为「灵魂，生命」。
semantic_path 第二站 how 补『指代人』义的确切起点（14 世纪初）与其修辞机制（以部分代全体），替换套话；词源深处『来自海/湖』的猜测按未定论口径只放 mechanism_sentence 并注明。
evidence: Etymonline: "Middle English soule, from Old English sawol \"spiritual and emotional part of a person, animate existence; life, living being,\" from Proto-Germanic *saiwalō, a word of uncertain origin. It has been suspected to have meant originally \"coming from or belonging to the sea,\" the supposed stopping place of the soul before birth or after death [Barnhart]... Klein explains this as \"from the lake,\" as a dwelling-place of souls in ancient northern Europe."
Etymonline: "As a synonym for \"person, individual, human being\" (as in every living soul) it dates from early 14c."
soul.mechanism_sentence: soul 是古英语 sāwol——「人身上的精神部分、生命本身」：14 世纪起，它以最要紧的部分代全体，直接指「人」（every living soul）；它更深的来历未定，有一说与「海」有关（古人信灵魂栖于水），来源只登记为猜测。

semantic_path.how: 以部分代全人（提喻）：14 世纪初起 soul 直接指『人、个体』（如 not a soul 一个人也没有）——拿人身上最要紧的那部分，称呼整个人；词库字面义『灵魂』仍是首站本义。

changes: original_meaning 与拉丁语 species 的首义对齐为「外观，外貌」（其『类』义是晚期拉丁语逻辑语言里的引申，现行路径缺这一层）。
semantic_path 按 Etymonline 重建三站（外观 → 晚期拉丁逻辑『属下之种』/14 世纪末入英语 → 约 1600 年生物学物种），how 写明『样子→凭据』的桥。
evidence: Etymonline: "species (n.) late 14c., in logic, \"a class of individuals or things,\" from Latin species \"a particular sort, kind, or type\" (opposed to genus), originally \"a sight, look, view; outward appearance, shape, form,\" a derivative of specere \"to look at, to see, behold\""

Etymonline: "In Late Latin, in logic and legal language, it acquired the meaning \"a special case,\" especially (as a translation of Greek eidos) \"a class included under a higher class; a kind; a sort...\" The English word is attested from 1560s as \"a distinct class (of something) based on common characteristics.\" The specific use in biological sciences in reference to groups of living things recognizably distinct from all others by their inherited characteristics is from c. 1600"
species.mechanism_sentence: species 出自拉丁语 specere「看」，本义是「看出来的那副样子」：逻辑学先拿这副样子当归类的凭据（属之下的「种」），约 1600 年生物学把它定死为「物种」。

semantic_path.how: 『样子』成了归类的凭据：晚期拉丁语里 species 在逻辑与法律语言中对译希腊语 eidos，指『大类（genus）之下、凭共同相貌特征分出的一类』；14 世纪末英语在逻辑学语境接过此义——词库泛义『种类』即此。
生物学把它钉死：约 1600 年 species 专指『凭遗传特征能与其他类群辨认区分的生物类群』——词库『物种』即此（Etymonline 附注：这一定义至今未有定论）。
